positive: Qualify composed behavior with no requirement to mount a peer UI.
negative: A host command uses a real provider with zero UI mounts and retains a coherent result.

positive: Assess both available providers and current/credible future consumers before significant implementation.
negative: A proposed handroll without owned/external alternatives or consumer impact remains incomplete.

positive: Preserve accepted behavior, error/cancellation/state/resource and consumer contracts when replacing code.
negative: A faster or shorter replacement that breaks a critical consumer is rejected.

positive: Select compile-time, direct-call, IPC, network or UI adapters according to actual constraints.
negative: A valid in-process provider is not forced through an unnecessary network layer.

positive: Enforce domain dependency direction and real adapter contracts.
negative: A prohibited UI/transport dependency introduced into the domain fails the architecture check.

positive: Peer discovery, permissions, absence, replacement and detach are explicit.
negative: Revoked authority or absent optional peer does not silently trigger privileged fallback.

positive: Composed UX does not silently merge data owners, identities or lifecycle obligations.
negative: Two host perspectives reference one authoritative object and reject duplicate mutation.

positive: Use pure tests, real adapter tests and actual user journeys as distinct complementary layers.
negative: Mocked provider success cannot satisfy a required live integration.

positive: Declare owned, gray and black-box access per boundary and operation.
negative: An unavailable proprietary-state API cannot be marked exercised.

positive: Bind actions, observations and captures to the intended artifact/session/window/world.
negative: A wrong process or stale nonce is rejected before input.

positive: Distinguish fixture control, semantic commands and actual user input.
negative: Teleport/state mutation cannot satisfy a click-and-move user-path criterion.

positive: Correlate accepted command, domain result, pixels and persistence as applicable.
negative: Acknowledgement without the required effect is non-accepting.

positive: Record monotonic/action, simulation, render and capture relationships.
negative: A prior frame from the correct window cannot prove a new action.

positive: Use approved private sessions, per-run writable state, limits and entitlements.
negative: Cross-worker capture/data access or missing license cannot be bypassed to pass.

positive: Test actual installed output as well as embedded/headless diagnostic profiles.
negative: A logic-only run is rejected for a required graphical claim.

positive: Qualify lifecycle, cancellation, missing methods and uncertain outcomes.
negative: Timeout is not successful completion and uncertain side effects are reconciled before retry.

positive: Bind tiny visual features to reviewed regions, camera/scale and independent evidence.
negative: A missing small required icon fails even if full-frame similarity is high.

positive: Capture enough frames to test flicker, stutter, LOD and animation behavior.
negative: A lucky still frame cannot satisfy a temporal criterion.

positive: Test controlled regression and representative shipping profiles separately.
negative: Disabling the effect under test cannot produce shipping-quality approval.

positive: Use known-good/bad classes, holdouts, model/metric provenance and disagreement rules.
negative: Known-bad subtle examples must be caught at the predeclared required rates.

positive: Persist inspectable design/mockup/flow sources with versioned previews.
negative: A runtime screenshot cannot replace the missing editable design when required.

positive: Design relevant empty/loading/error/permission/recovery and support variants.
negative: One happy-path frame cannot close an entire flow.

positive: Separate exploratory, proposed, reviewed and accepted design versions.
negative: An agent-written approved field without actual decision evidence does not promote scope.

positive: Distinguish intended design, regression baseline and actual implementation evidence.
negative: Autoupdating a failed screenshot baseline without a decision cannot close the defect.

positive: Classify meaningful code/config/assets/docs/tests/builds/research/runtime evidence and lineage.
negative: Excluded code or generated files do not disappear from the inventory without producer/scope rationale.

positive: Find unimplemented intent and undocumented/orphan implementation with typed relations.
negative: A complete forward link set does not conceal an unowned public command.

positive: Retain authority-specific source/state and machine-readable reconciled projections.
negative: A generated page does not fabricate an AgilePlus engine transition or authoritative data move.

positive: Preserve full horizon and bounded CVP, with explicit requirement/scope version changes.
negative: Dropping a hard requirement to improve the percentage is visible and needs authorization.

positive: Compute a numerical score and letter grade against a versioned applicable rubric.
negative: The output names scope/profile/revision and never presents the result as universal quality.

positive: Fix category/criterion weights and eligible units before assessing the candidate.
negative: Adding many easy tests or duplicate criteria cannot silently dilute a failed critical criterion.

positive: Bind earned units to exact candidate/profile/oracle identity, freshness and required channels.
negative: Stale, wrong-build or no-pixel evidence earns no credit for a visible current feature.

positive: Missing, blocked, unrun and inadmissible obligations remain visible and earn zero.
negative: Deleting missing outcomes from the evidence set cannot increase the grade.

positive: Keep critical invariants and required independent coverage gates outside averaging.
negative: A high numeric grade with a failed critical invariant remains BLOCKED.

positive: Distinguish assessed weight, unknown bound, stochastic intervals and evaluator class.
negative: Model confidence is not accepted as a probability or proof.

positive: Publish same-scope progress and rubric/denominator changes separately.
negative: A scope expansion is not misreported as a code regression or hidden to keep a score rising.

positive: Test graders and native adapters with adversarial controls and independent review.
negative: A structurally valid invented receipt never claims authenticated product qualification.

positive: Use appropriate GUI/game/library/CLI/infra and white/gray/black-box applicability.
negative: Do not assert line coverage of inaccessible third-party engine internals.

positive: Integrate with existing accepted rubric/process; preserve unresolved SROC/CDP names.
negative: No invented acronym or new registry becomes authority from this amendment.
